extracted.intended_audience: patent proprietors, patent attorneys, IP litigators and in-house counsel considering UPC strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the finalised Unified Patent Court Rules of Procedure (in force 1 Sept 2022) with practical implications for opting-out European patents, videoconference hearings, and public access to court documents. Aimed at helping proprietors and advisers understand procedural requirements and risks when preparing for UPC litigation or opt-out decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opting-out must cover all designated states for which patent granted (Rule 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 5(1)(b) amended to specify that an application to opt out a European patent must be made in respect of all designated states for which the European patent has been granted, rather than just the Contracting Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically this means opt-out (and withdrawal of opt-out, e.g. Rule 5.7) must be made in respect of all states in which the patent has been granted, including EPC states not participating in the UPC (e.g. UK, Spain, Switzerland). The explanatory notes say the previous wording was inconsistent with the indivisibility of the application to opt out. The change increases complexity of the opt-out procedure and means opt-outs require a high degree of care because an opt-out may be ineffective if not completed correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism to remove unauthorised opt-outs/withdrawals (Rule 5A)
rubrics_metrics.description: New Rule 5A provides a mechanism for proprietors of European patents to apply to remove unauthorised opt-outs or unauthorised withdrawals of opt-outs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietors may file a reasoned application to have an unauthorised opt-out/withdrawal deleted; the Registrar will delete the unauthorised entry if the application is deemed acceptable. This addresses concerns arising from the lack of identity checks on proprietors listed in opt-out/withdrawal applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Videoconference hearings allowed, including fully remote hearings in exceptional circumstances (Rule 112(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 112.3 enables the court to allow a party, representative, or witness to attend a hearing by videoconference and permits oral hearings to be conducted entirely by videoconference if all parties agree or if 'the Court considers it appropriate to do so in exceptional circumstances.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of exceptional circumstances in the explanatory notes include travel restrictions and 'disproportionality' (e.g. a long journey for simple and short oral proceedings). Unlike the EPO pilot where ViCo is default, parties must request ViCo at the UPC. Regardless of format, hearings will be transmitted to the courtroom so members of the public can view proceedings, thereby respecting the 'principle of publicity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to written pleadings and evidence restricted; access upon reasoned request (Rule 262)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 262 amended so that written pleadings and evidence on the register 'shall be available to the public upon reasoned request to the Registry' rather than being freely accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registry will consult parties before granting a request, and any release is subject to confidentiality requests. This approach departs from the EPO where register documents are freely accessible and is driven by GDPR compliance. The practical effect is currently uncertain — it remains to be seen what level of justification will be required for a successful access request. Separately, all decisions and orders of the Court will be published, subject to redaction of personal data and confidentiality requests; the extent of redaction may affect the utility of published decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted access to commercially sensitive information and trade secrets (Rule 262A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 262A enables parties to request that access to certain information necessary for the proceedings (e.g. commercially sensitive information or trade secrets) be restricted to certain specified individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must provide justification for the restriction; the other party may respond; the court will decide whether the applicant's reasons 'significantly outweigh' the other party's interest in full access. Complete restriction is not possible under Rule 262A.6: at least one natural person nominated by each party, as well as their representative, must be able to access the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of publicity for hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of whether hearings are in-person or by videoconference, hearings will be transmitted to the courtroom to enable members of the public to view proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the 'principle of publicity' even when parts or all of hearings are conducted remotely. When requesting ViCo, parties and the court must bear in mind arrangements that allow public access to the proceedings.
